pageCache.pageTitle: Home - St Mary's C of E Primary School Twickenham
pageCache.text:
St Mary’s is a church school with a vision to achieve excellence balanced with compassion. Christian values and beliefs form the basis of our school ethos and are reflected in our teaching and in the daily life of the school.
Very importantly, we have a strong sense of community where all members of the school are encouraged to respect and value each other.
St Mary’s is also very much part of the wider community in Twickenham. The history of the school dates back to 1645, so we have a long and successful tradition of providing education for local children.
ADMISSIONS
RELIGIOUS ETHOS
St Mary’s CE Primary School was visited by Ofsted for an inspection on 16th and 17th November 2023 and received an ‘Outstanding’ judgement. Please find the report here:
Ofsted report 2023
We received our Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) visit on 1st December 2023 and received a judgement where St Mary’s CE Primary School was found to be ‘living up to its foundation as a Church school’. Please find the report here:
SIAMS report 2023
ADMISSIONS

Ofsted report 2023

SIAMS report 2023
ADMISSIONS
RELIGIOUS ETHOS
St Mary’s CE Primary School was visited by Ofsted for an inspection on 16th and 17th November 2023 and received an ‘Outstanding’ judgement. Please find the report here:
Ofsted report 2023
We received our Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) visit on 1st December 2023 and received a judgement where St Mary’s CE Primary School was found to be ‘living up to its foundation as a Church school’. Please find the report here:
SIAMS report 2023
St Mary’s school values: kindness, caring for and helping others, working together for example. There is a sense of calm throughout the school. All pupils receive an excellent education.
My child gets the support she needs. Teachers have a positive and proactive approach. The school is well maintained and is pleasant to visit. I like the fact that learning is supplemented with relevant school trips.
Pupils are often given a platform for their voices and opinions, whether through assemblies or classroom show and tell. The confidence of the children as a result is great.
There is an excellent “no bullying” policy and “sharing is caring” policy. We value the “friendship” stop and the helpful and caring receptionists. St Mary’s has amazing teachers.
Front line staff, communication with parents, a strong school relationship within the community.
Christian values are embedded in the culture of the school, not just given lip-service, plus there is a desire to create a nurturing environment in which every child is valued.
St Mary’s has a strong inclusive policy embracing pupils of all faiths and abilities. The expectation is that children are kind caring and considerate to everyone. This has always made St Marys children stand out from other schools which is especially noticeable on school trips.
St Mary’s has clear, strong leadership; great teachers who seem to care about what they do plus a committed PTA and involvement in the local community
The split site nature of the school makes the children feel safe as they enter in reception, but also ensures they feel part of a whole school environment. The teachers have a very open policy and communicate well to enable all parents, even those who work full time, feel involved in their children’s schooling. Mrs Abrahams has brought a refreshing, professional yet personal approach to communicating with the parents. The support staff on each site are very approachable and efficient. The standard of teaching is consistently high across all sites and the facilities are good for a London type school.
St Mary’s is a nurturing, caring, compassionate school with a strong educational environment and great handwriting!
The children are guided to grow personally, academically, morally, socially and spiritually in an inspiring, beautiful and safe environment. At the core of our vision is a determination to foster, in all children, a love of learning that will endure long after they leave us, enabling them to adapt easily to whatever future challenges they may meet throughout their lives.
St Mary’s is a three form, three site school with excellent teaching and learning resources on each site: Amyand Park Road for Reception and Year 1, Strafford Road for Years 2 and 3 and Richmond Road houses Years 4, 5 and 6.
PARENT SURVEY FEEDBACK
My child is happy at this school 94%
My child feels safe at this school 96%
My child enjoys their learning at school 95%

GOVERNANCE
St Mary’s has a long and distinguished history and through its willingness to evolve and be flexible, it will have an equally bright and exciting future. Our mission statement is: “Growing and learning together, inspired by Jesus’ love”, our motto “Conemur” (we will try), and our aspiration for every member of the school community to follow the example of Mary our patron in being compassionate, loving, caring and inclusive. This is a school with excellent relationships between and among adults and learners; the SIAMS Inspector in February 2016 commended the shared commitment of leaders and governors and chaplain which is “sustaining a culture that blends compassion with excellence”.
SCHOOL GOVERNORS
STRATEGIC PLAN
2022: St Mary’s will be a centre of excellence locally and nationally, a beacon catering for the needs of all children and celebrating their diversity. Our 630 pupils, spread over 3 sites, will thrive in a small school familiarity whilst belonging to one cohesive school with shared Christian values and a common identity. Ethos Statement
Growing and learning together to be our best, inspired by Jesus’ love.
At St Mary’s we seek to:
Nurture our children and every member of the school community with a sense of God by encouraging deeper relationships between each other and with God, helping to make Him more real for all of us.
As Mary, our patron, brought Jesus into our world for every one of us, the aspiration of the school is to follow her example through compassion, love, care and inclusivity.
St Mary’s children and staff, strive to live out the words of the Bible we hold so sacred: ‘True love shows itself in action” (1 John 3:18)

Our Values
Our values
Our values enhance and enrich our vision; we celebrate excellence through Endurance, Wisdom and Service and encourage compassion through Friendship, Thankfulness and Forgiveness.
The below artwork was created by some of our most able artists alongside some of our talented staff artists. Each value is linked to one specific Bible story which is shared with the children every year. The words below are how our children have articulated the meaning of each value.
We created videos for each of our Christian values. We hope these videos help you to see how they come to life everyday here at St Mary’s.
ENDURANCE
Courage to give it a go even when it’s tough; never giving up; building character through resilience and perseverance.
View Video
WISDOM
Gaining the wisdom, knowledge and skills to make the right choices; reflecting on our strengths and areas for development; learning from our experiences to make a difference.
View Video
FORGIVENESS
Showing compassion for others, realising we all make mistakes and becoming stronger for them.
View Video
SERVICE
Working for ourselves and one another, committing to our work; learning from and being inspired by Jesus Christ.
View Video
FRIENDSHIP
Learning to work well with others; loving one another; treating each other with dignity and respect.
View Video
THANKFULNESS
Appreciating ourselves, each other and our world; valuing our learning opportunities; showing gratitude and saying ‘thank you’.
View Video

pageCache.text:
St Mary’s Church
St Mary’s School has strong links with St Mary’s Church in Twickenham. Father Jeff regularly visits school for Collective Worships and celebrations and the children, staff and wider school c0mmunity visit and use the church throughout the year.
St Mary’s Church
Father Jeff Vicar at St Mary’s Church, Twickenham
Father Jeff Hopkin Williams started life in Llanelli, Wales, where he attended a primary school very similar to St Mary’s. Father Jeff attended Chichester Theological College, which was affilliated to Southampton University, and completed a Theology degree. On completion of his studies, Father Jeff took up his first official post within the Church as Assistant Curate in Eastbourne. He progressed to the role of Rector at Upper St Leonards near Hastings where he was Chaplain to a hospice for eight years. The parish of St Mary’s, Twickenham, welcomed Jeff as our Vicar in March 2002.
Father Jeff is a vibrant and welcoming figure in the life of the children at school, seeing each child as an individual. Through regular collective worships in school, and opening the Church doors to the parents, friends and families of our children, Father Jeff has become an integral part of our small community, and enriched it for all.
Father Jeff also works with other Trustees at St Mary’s to secure a solid financial foundation for our school to carry on growing and thriving into the future. During his spare time, he enjoys writing short stories, collecting art, listening to Jazz music and wlaking his dogs around Twickenham and the Sussex countryside.
In 2023, Father Jeff had a book published called ‘The Anatomy of Shadows’ where he details how the area came through Covid-19. The book examines ‘how to create a sense of community, when that community is not allowed to meet’.
Please read more about the church on their website St Mary’s Church website

Wraparound childcare: SMASH
WELCOME
WELCOME
Welcome to our highly regarded school-run wraparound care provision, St Mary’s After School Hub, known as ‘SMASH’.
We are delighted to offer childcare provision for all pupils of St Mary’s School.
We offer a variety of childcare solutions:
– Term time childcare for regular or occasional booking
– Holiday and INSET Day sessions
Our Prices
We are proud to continue to offer the lowest cost childcare in the local area.
Breakfast Club – £7 per session
After School Club – £26 per session (Ts & Cs apply)
Our Aim
We strive to provide a safe environment with a focus on fun with a broad range of activities that the children will want to come back to. We aim to ensure the children feel relaxed and at home in a friendly, warm, caring environment. Children are encouraged to take part in activities which will stimulate and encourage personal development.
Our flexible space allows us to accommodate a large number of children whilst maintaining a high staff to child ratio.
What Our Current Parents Say
Making a Booking
Please see our Booking Request Forms below. During the Summer Term, we have a dedicated form for new Reception children starting in September.
Regular term-time bookings are taken on an on-going basis and are payable in advance monthly. Our club runs on the Middle Site and pupils attending SMASH during school term are escorted to and/or from our club no matter which school site they attend.
Ad Hoc bookings for occasional sessions are subject to availability and are payable in advance upon our booking confirmation to you.
Our INSET day and school holiday provisions are bookable as separate items and Booking Request Forms are available as the occasions arise.
Links to Booking Request Forms and Information
Parents’ Involvement
Smash welcomes parental involvement and we aim to forge and strengthen relationships with parents so we maintain excellent levels of communication at all times. The partnership between children, the club and parents is important to us and helps us to provide the very best care for your child.
We ensure equal opportunity for all our children and families, regardless of their race, religion, culture, disability or social background.
Contact Us
Please look at our Terms and Conditions for full information about the club or if you have a specific question, our FAQs will probably have the answer you need. If you require more information, please don’t hesitate to contact us at:

pageCache.pageTitle: Training & Careers at St Mary's - St Mary's C of E Primary School Twickenham
pageCache.text:
Training & Careers at St Mary’s
What is it like to work at St Mary’s? St Mary’s Church of England Primary School is a popular and inclusive three-form entry school in central Twickenham, deemed Outstanding by Ofsted. We are split over three sites with good local transport links. We promote a caring Christian ethos that is fully dedicated to developing every child. Our energetic and welcoming team enthuse and motivate pupils to strive for success. We deliver high quality lessons while successfully nurturing and inspiring pupils to reach their full potential. Our creative curriculum, themed around topics of learning, not only engages pupils and fosters a love of learning but also enthuses our teaching team to plan and deliver exciting and meaningful lessons. Behaviour is excellent with pupils demonstrating respect and good manners to adults and peers alike. We have access to excellent CPD opportunities to grow and develop through mentorship and coaching. Such is our size and structure, there are good prospects for both new and experienced practitioners who want to progress into leadership roles. Importantly, we highly value both pupil and staff wellbeing; we know that to continue to be successful, we need a happy, healthy team.
St Mary’s staff with children of their own are given priority in our Admissions Policy criteria. Early Career Teachers (ECTs) are well supported; our ECT programme is delivered by the Wandle Teaching Hub through UCL (see our ECT policy for further information).
Training opportunities at St Mary’s We are committed to supporting the development of future teachers, whether they go on to work at St Mary’s or not. We want to share our best practice and our vision for primary education with the teachers of tomorrow. We have a close relationship with St Mary’s University and support placements for their trainee teachers from both their PGCE and B. Ed. programmes.
In addition, St Mary’s CE Primary School works in conjunction with Teaching London: LDBS SCITT, to recruit and train teachers on the School Direct programme leading to Qualified Teacher Status (QTS) and a Postgraduate Certificate in Education (PGCE). School Direct is a school-based route into teaching. As a School Direct trainee training with our school and our ITT provider, Teaching London, you will learn alongside inspiring, passionate teachers with outstanding pedagogical knowledge. You will be trained to become a successful, confident and effective teacher, and will be equipped to teach in a dynamic and vibrant primary school. You will undertake entirely ‘on the job’ teacher training, allowing you to gain the qualifications and practical skills required to become a teacher.
Entry Requirements Teaching London is seeking high quality graduates who can demonstrate a commitment to teaching as a career. To find out more about our entry requirements, click here.
How to Apply Candidates should apply via gov.uk. Course codes are available here. Applicants who are successful at interview will be offered a conditional place.

pageCache.pageTitle: Languages - St Mary's C of E Primary School Twickenham
pageCache.text:
Languages
Languages
St Mary’s is a school that celebrates languages. We have children from a variety of backgrounds for whom English is an Additional Language (typically over 35 languages spoken) and we celebrate and take great interest in that – one of the many benefits from living in London. Children learn French at St Mary’s. In Reception, Year 1 and Year 2, they are exposed to the French language regularly through singing songs, French signs around school and a whole school French Day. Formal lessons begin in Year 3, in line with National Curriculum expectations. Children progress from learning simple phrases and recording simple words in Year 3 to having simple conversations, writing sentences and reading more confidently by the end of Year 6. More than anything, we aim to instil a love and enthusiasm for languages.
There are also language clubs allowing languages to be practised and enjoyed across the school, available to some of our younger children too.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mathematics - St Mary's C of E Primary School Twickenham
pageCache.text:
Mathematics
Mathematics
We know that confidence in mathematics is crucial. We ensure quality time is given to develop a true sense of Number in all year groups. This is especially true in the younger years where concrete resources play a vital role in developing conceptual understandings of key mathematics areas. Knowing the importance of Times Tables, we aspire for all our pupils to be fluent in their recitation and application by the end of Year 4. Every day, throughout the school, we ensure our pupils have the opportunity to count or practise their Times Tables.
Equally important as Number confidence is the application of mathematical methods to solving problems. Reasoning skills are developed frequently so our pupils develop the language and strategies to solve challenging problems and know how to apply written and mental methods when solving them. This ability to solve ‘real-life’ problems not only helps makes sense of learning, putting it into context, but also prepares us for future careers and everyday use of mathematics.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - St Mary's C of E Primary School Twickenham
pageCache.text:
Music
Music
At St Mary’s we aim to instil a lifelong love and appreciation for music. Pupils enter Collective Worships listening to musicians from different genres of music, exposing them to the richness of both modern and classical music. Singing Collective Worships are led by a music specialist to ensure high quality outcomes alongside the emotional and spiritual wellbeing achieved through choral performances. Our school choirs enable pupils to develop and showcase their talents. We work closely alongside Richmond Music Arts to provide instrument tuition: all Year 2 pupils learn to play the recorder and all Year 4 pupils learn a brass instrument. Weekly lessons develop the key skills of listening, performing and evaluating music. As pupils progress though the school, they further explore how music is created including dynamics, structure and musical notations.

pageCache.pageTitle: Science - St Mary's C of E Primary School Twickenham
pageCache.text:
Science
Science
At St Mary’s we deliver a creative, engaging and challenging curriculum that encourages curiosity whilst progressively building skills (working scientifically), knowledge and understanding on previously learnt content – pupils will know more, remember more and do more. Every lesson involves a practical element, developing skills, knowledge and a fascination with science. Investigation write-ups progress in depth, language and scientific understanding as pupils get older; as pupils move up the school, they are given further opportunities to design and carry out their own investigations. There is a strong focus and expectation to use precise scientific language as we strive for academic excellence. St Mary’s strives to fill pupils with curiosity and wonder about their world, and delight when they have the opportunity to investigate, explore and create. We learn the skills of explanation, prediction and analysis, hoping that the future scientists, doctors, nurses and Nobel Prize winners start here.
